skill.name: ai-runtime-toolkit
skill.description: AI Runtime Toolkit helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code discover and run local development tools for code analysis, service checks, API testing, and CLI workflows.
skill.summary: Discover, organize, and run internal and external developer tools from one AI-assisted toolkit.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms several real risks around pipe-to-shell installation guidance, sudo setup commands, environment-file sourcing, subprocess execution, shell configuration changes, and filesystem writes. Many other static matches are documentation links, JavaScript template literals, localhost examples, or normal diagnostic shell patterns and were adjudicated as false positives. No additional prompt-injection or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found beyond the static evidence.

remediation.issue: Pipe-to-shell installer guidance appears in multiple external tool references.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell instructions with package-manager installation, checksum verification, or explicit download-and-review steps.

remediation.issue: Several setup examples require sudo or modify user shell startup files.
remediation.suggestion: Move privileged setup into clearly marked manual steps and require user confirmation before any command changes system or shell configuration.

remediation.issue: The service check script sources a .env file directly.
remediation.suggestion: Parse only required key-value settings without executing shell syntax, and avoid printing or forwarding secrets.

remediation.issue: The toolkit can execute registered external commands and write report files.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain executable paths, validate arguments, show commands before execution, and write outputs only to explicit user-approved paths.

content.value_statement: Development teams often lose time finding the right local tool for analysis, testing, or service checks. This skill provides a structured toolkit that helps AI assistants discover available tools and run common developer workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists internal Python, Bash, and Node.js tools with metadata and usage examples.
Runs selected toolkit commands through a discovery CLI when the local environment permits execution.
Documents service health checks, disk checks, log analysis, API testing, and code statistics workflows.
Describes external CLI integrations such as fzf, ripgrep, jq, bat, eza, zoxide, and starship.
Provides reference guides for creating new toolkit tools and organizing tool metadata.
limitations: Some workflows execute shell commands and need careful review before use on sensitive systems.
External tool installation instructions may require manual verification and trusted sources.
The toolkit depends on local operating system tools that may not be installed.
Documentation examples may need adaptation for each project and security policy.

use_cases.title: Inspect a development environment
use_cases.description: Use the toolkit to find available local tools for service checks, disk analysis, and dependency inspection.

use_cases.title: Standardize project diagnostics
use_cases.description: Give contributors a single place to discover diagnostic commands and reusable analysis workflows.

use_cases.title: Test APIs during development
use_cases.description: Run documented API test flows against local or approved endpoints and export readable results.

prompt_templates.title: Find available tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me what tools this AI Runtime Toolkit provides and group them by purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a diagnostic workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to diagnose a slow local service. Which toolkit tools should I use first, and what should each one tell me?

prompt_templates.title: Run a safe local check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the toolkit to check a local service health endpoint. Explain any command before running it and avoid external network calls.

prompt_templates.title: Audit tool integration risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the toolkit external integration guidance for commands that install software, modify shell startup files, or execute downloaded scripts.

output_examples.input: Find tools for checking whether my local API is healthy.
output_examples.output: The toolkit identifies the service check and API test workflows, explains their expected inputs, and highlights that local endpoints are safer than external targets.

output: Search and selection tools are documented.
File viewing and JSON processing tools are documented.
Installation guidance should be reviewed before use.

output_examples.input: Prepare a safe onboarding note for this toolkit.
output_examples.output: The response explains tool discovery, local-only testing, approval before shell execution, and review of any installation command.

best_practices: Review each shell command before execution, especially commands that install software or modify shell configuration.
Prefer local endpoints and test data when using API and service-check workflows.
Verify external tool sources through official package managers or trusted release channels.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe downloaded installer scripts directly into a shell without inspection.
Do not run toolkit commands against production systems without explicit approval.
Do not store secrets in files that toolkit scripts source or print during diagnostics.

faq.question: Does this skill install external tools automatically?
faq.answer: It documents external tool installation methods, but users should review and approve any installation command first.

faq.question: Can it run API tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Node.js API testing workflow that can target a configured base URL.

faq.question: Is it limited to Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What types of tools are included?
faq.answer: The toolkit includes Python analysis tools, Bash system tools, Node.js API tools, and external CLI references.

faq.question: Can this be used on production systems?
faq.answer: Use caution. Production use should require explicit approval, reviewed commands, and least-privilege access.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: Several examples execute shell commands, source environment files, or recommend pipe-to-shell installers.
